We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work, having been named among the 100 Best Companies to Work For in Seattle Business Magazine and Washington’s Best Workplaces in the Puget Sound Business Journal. Who we're looking for:
We are seeking a Business Analyst on the Finance Analytics team that will be the go-to person for financial metric decomposition and narration, ultimately directly influencing business outcomes and strategic priorities, and forward-looking modeling of our repeat customers, partnering with Finance to both maintain the models and narrate performance against forecast. 
As a Business Analyst on the Finance Analytics team, you will work with the broader Finance organization and Product Analytics team to analyze and narrate our marketplace. You are proactive about identifying positive and negative changes in financial metrics while also working with the team to hypothesize, investigate, and identify the underlying root cause of fluctuations in our metrics. This position requires a professional in data storytelling: we are looking for someone who is capable of presenting trends and overarching narratives of business performance to the broader organization, including senior leadership. 
As a Business Analyst, you will also partner with Accounting, Tax and Product to maintain current reporting on various areas of the business, and are also encouraged to identify opportunities to improve reporting to better meet the teams’ needs. When there are changes across the business that impact Finance, including product feature experiments, new business lines, and regulatory changes, you will partner with stakeholders, both technical and non-technical, to find the right solution.
 This is a hybrid position that has the minimum expectation to work out of our Downtown Seattle Office two days per week on Mondays and Thursdays. For this reason, candidates must be based in the Greater Seattle Area.
Additionally, applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis, without the need for current or future employer sponsorship for an employment-based visa status.

lists.content:
• Become a subject matter expert on database queries related to all payments and finance tables, cohort modeling, and integrated third-party vendor data.

  • Monitor existing metrics and build new metrics that will drive business impact.

  • Regularly present to senior leadership and the finance organization on the trends and insights into changes in the business. This includes the decomposition of the drivers of those changes as well as recommendations on actions to improve marketplace performance.

  • Provide leverage for the finance, accounting, and tax teams through insights, narratives and increased automation/simplification. Be a thought partner for business owners, getting to the question behind the question and distilling the underlying need to analyze data.

  • Demonstrate flexibility and a collaborative mindset by stepping in to support teammates and cross-functional partners as needed.

• 3+ years business experience in Analytics.

  • Background in data-informed decision-making and partnering with multi-functional teams.

  • Track record of strong written and verbal communication to construct clear data narratives to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leadership.

  • Familiarly with finance and accounting principles, including financial statements.

  • Fluent with SQL and data visualization tools (e.g. Tableau, Looker, etc.) to independently conduct root cause analyses. 

  • Experience working with data infrastructure / engineering teams to build and optimize data models. 

  • Experience working with Python, R, or a similar computational language.
• Experience in a two-sided marketplace.

• Competitive compensation

  • 401k match

  • Flexible PTO

  • Competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Commuter benefits

  • Bring your dog to work (and unlimited puppy time)

  • Doggy benefits, including $1000 toward adopting your first dog

  • Stocked fridges, coffee, soda, and lots of treats (for humans and dogs) and free catered lunches semi-monthly 

  • Regular team activities performed in-person and virtually

• In the greater Seattle area the first-year salary range is $83,931-$108,167. Additionally, Rover offers benefits to full-time employees.
  • The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.

lists.content:
• Work with the VP of Corporate Development and other key internal stakeholders to evaluate, negotiate, and execute acquisitions and strategic partnerships

  • Develop investment theses and strategic rationale for potential acquisitions 

  • Build target financial models including forecast scenarios, synergies, and integration costs

  • Coach and develop junior team members on financial modeling and deal process

  • Apply a deep understanding of Rover’s business and operating environment to inform deal evaluation

  • Partner with the integrations lead to develop integration plans and success criteria for transactions

  • Drive post-close evaluation of completed transactions against success criteria

  • Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of external targets that can accelerate Rover’s businesses

  • Monitor the pet industry ecosystem, including existing and emerging players

  • Establish relationships with founders, executives, and decision-makers at relevant companies

• 10+ years of corporate development and/or M&A experience, whether in-house or in investment banking / advisory

  • Proven ability to develop and articulate the strategic value of potential transactions 

  • Strong financial modeling skills, including forecasting, synergy estimation and sensitivity analysis of targets

  • Ability to identify, articulate, and pressure-test key financial and strategic assumptions underlying potential acquisitions

  • Project and stakeholder management skills across the full deal lifecycle, including identification, financial evaluation, due diligence, negotiation, integration, and retrospective analysis

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Ability to build trusted internal and external relationships 

  • Ability to develop an understanding of individual companies as well as their place within an industry ecosystem

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Accounting, Finance, or a related field

• Experience in the technology or pet sectors

  • MBA or equivalent advanced degree

• Competitive compensation
  • 401k match
  • Long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout
  • Flexible PTO
  • Competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Commuter benefits
  • Bring your dog to work (and unlimited puppy time)
  • Pet benefits, including $1000 toward adopting your first dog or cat
  • Stocked fridges, coffee, soda, and lots of treats (for humans and dogs) and free catered lunches monthly  
  • Regular team activities performed in-person and virtually

• In the greater Seattle area the first-year salary range is $178,513 - $220,822 with a 15% bonus. Additionally, Rover offers benefits to full-time employees.
  • The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.

lists.content:
Rover is looking for a Director of Pet Parent Journey & GTM to join our Pet Parent Organization. In this role, you will build and drive consistent go-to-market strategies and initiatives for all pet parent–facing investments, you will own pet parent communications strategy, alignment, and execution, and you will own the message architecture and journey documentation that every pet parent touch point ladders up to.

This will include owning the end-to-end global positioning, messaging, and channel strategies for the pet parent product roadmap and initiatives. This is a high-impact role that requires a unique blend of strategic vision and hands-on execution. You will be equally comfortable aligning executive stakeholders on long-term journey strategy as you are digging into the day-to-day decisions that determine whether a pet parent books, returns, and stays.

You own the strategy across the areas below. Execution is delivered hand-in-hand with cross-functional partners, and your job is to define what good looks like, set the framework, hold the alignment, and make sure the pieces reinforce each other rather than fragmenting by team, brand, market, or channel.

  • Pet parent GTM. The end-to-end strategy for taking demand-side initiatives to market: positioning, channels, messaging, sequencing, and measurement, applied consistently across services, brands, and countries. You will partner with Product, UX, Marketing, International, and brand teams to ensure its effective and scalable execution.

  • Pet parent communications. A unified communications strategy: voice, segmentation, cadence, governance, quality bar, across both UX and non-UX touch points. You will partner with Lifecycle, Product, UX, and International to ensure its effective execution.

  • Message architecture and journey documentation. The brand-aligned message pillars for pet parents and the single source of truth that all journey content must ladder up to, reviewed at launch and audited for consistency across live journeys.

  • Consideration and the active shopper. The alignment between off-platform communications and the active shopper journey in UX, so that lifecycle and consideration are developed as one plan rather than two that get reconciled after the fact. You will partner with UX, Lifecycle, and Performance Marketing.

  • Pet parent voice and feedback. The strategy and the mechanisms by which pet parent sentiment, feedback, and lived experience are measured, surfaced, and acted on. You define the signals, set the cadence, and hold the company accountable to what pet parents tell us. You will partner with Data Science, UX Research, Product, and Operations.

• 10+ years of experience in one or more of the following fields: product marketing, B2C go-to-market, lifecycle or CRM leadership, product management, marketing, general management, or consulting roles in marketplace, platform, or two-sided business contexts.

  • Experience partnering with Product, UX, Data Science, and Engineering teams to create and execute on shared roadmaps and metrics.

  • Clear and structured written and verbal communication style, with the ability to influence and partner with senior leaders and diverse teams to drive critical decisions.

  • Highly proactive, comfortable operating with minimal guidance in uncertain and ambiguous business environments.

  • Analytical rigor, with enthusiasm for modeling and measuring the impact of the initiatives you drive, including incrementality and holdout-based measurement. 

  • Strong leadership skills and experience giving actionable feedback and coaching, and welcoming the same.

  • Comfortable working across US (Pacific Time) and Europe (Central European Time) timezones.

  • Bachelor’s degree. Marketing or business degrees preferred.

• Experience in online marketplaces with a meaningful consumer demand side (services marketplaces, accommodation, mobility, delivery, e-commerce, or similar).

  • Demonstrated track record of growing the demand side of a marketplace at scale: acquiring, activating, converting, and retaining customers against business targets.

  • Experience running lifecycle or CRM programs as a cross-channel system rather than an email channel, including next best action or triggered journey work.

  • Experience building go-to-market frameworks from scratch and getting other functions to adopt them.

  • Experience with customer advocacy, community, or advisory programs.

  • Master’s degree.

• Competitive compensation
  • 401k match
  • Long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout
  • Flexible PTO
  • Competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Commuter benefits
  • Bring your dog to work (and unlimited puppy time)
  • Pet benefits, including $1000 toward adopting your first dog or cat
  • Stocked fridges, coffee, soda, and lots of treats (for humans and dogs) and free catered lunches monthly  
  • Regular team activities performed in-person and virtually

• In the greater Seattle area the first-year salary range is $172,779 - $229,797 with a 15% bonus. Additionally, Rover offers benefits to full-time employees.

  • The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.

We’re investing in AI as a business accelerator and provide every team member access to AI tools in service of creating better experiences for our community.
We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work, having been named among the 100 Best Companies to Work For in Seattle Business Magazine and Washington’s Best Workplaces in the Puget Sound Business Journal. At Rover we’re committed to creating an accessible, inclusive, and welcoming community, which starts with our employees.
Want to make an impact? Join our pack and come work (and play!) with us.


Meet the team:
Our mighty team of four Application Analysts support the CRM and ERP applications that Rover relies on to handle customer contact. This means you'll have the opportunity to work with a broad cross-section of Rover team members, on initiatives that really make a difference for customers and employees. Our current tech stack is Zendesk for core CRM and Netsuite for ERP functions. All of our supported apps are multi-tenant, cloud-based, i.e. no on-prem servers.

Who we're looking for:
This role will provide technical understanding and support for Rover's CRM tools - specifically Zendesk. They will participate, directly and at a high skill level, in resolving technical issues within our owned platforms, coordinating the implementation of new features and functionality, and collaborating with partner teams on projects and initiatives. The position calls for a highly qualified, self-motivated employee who has a zeal for improving Rover’s internal and external customer experience, a wide and deep understanding of all aspects of the Zendesk platform, and a drive for efficiency and process improvement.

lists.content:
•  Evaluate Rover’s use of Zendesk and adjacent applications, and take a leadership role in defining and championing work to improve efficiency and optimize our implementation
  • Act as technical lead (if not full project lead) for efforts impacting our supported applications, helping to drive planning and solution design, as well as performing and/or facilitating configuration and other implementation work. These will include large feature rollouts, migrations, integrations, and optimization efforts.
  • Action Rover-internal issues and requests escalated by team’s front-line support analyst, prioritizing according to business impact, balancing against project work, and resolving or implementing them in a timely manner
  • Maintain expert-level technical understanding of supported applications, with a focus on identifying and surfacing features with potential to elevate Rover’s processes and outcomes
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to junior team members, helping them grow in understanding, in their role and along their career path
  • Supply thought leadership to operations and internal product roadmaps and other planning exercises, as well as flagging opportunities to increase our platforms’ usability, scalability, and efficiency
  • Provide domain expertise to partner teams and leadership, clarifying platform capabilities and preferred solutions

• Bachelor's degree or, in lieu of a degree, comparable relevant work experience
  • 5+ years direct experience administering and optimizing Zendesk implementations for established businesses, ideally with international footprints, including direct technical leadership of substantial efforts to build or iterate on complex functionality within that platform
  • Deep, detailed understanding of Zendesk and its configuration components (Triggers, Macros, Tags, Skills, Omnichannel
  • Routing including custom queues, etc.), as well as how it/they are used to support Operations teams for large-volume businesses
  • Strong familiarity with the Zendesk APIs and how these are used by software teams and other stakeholders to extract data, as well as executing actions against the Zendesk platform
  • Ability to understand business processes and translate business requirements into application functionality, including the ability to effectively and compassionately seek clarity from non-technical collaborators
  • Ability to operate independently and effectively without direct oversight (your manager and the rest of the team will be in Seattle), and prioritize your own work in response to evolving business needs
  • Curious, creative, and driven technologist with well-honed project management/participant, multitasking, and communication skills
  • Ability to apply technology to address practical business problems
  • Ability to balance attention to detail with expeditious execution in a fast-paced environment
  • Dedicated teammate who owns details and looks around corners, and who exemplifies a customer- and solutions-focused approach to challenges
  • Good communication capabilities across a variety of channels

• Zendesk Certified Administrator or Expert cerficiation
  • Experience working with scripting languages such as Python or JavaScript, and/or software development experience generally
  • Experience using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Rovo, etc.) to accelerate analysis and solution development, particularly in the context of Zendesk
  • Experience with at least one (and ideally more) M&A-driven migrations/integrations into Zendesk
  • Experience with Zendesk’s AI feature-set
  • General IT administration/support experience (managing email services/accounts, working with identity management systems like Okta, etc.)
  • Active participant in at least one RFP, RFI, and/or RFQ
  • Experience operating in Google Workspace toolset (Gmail/Calendar/Drive)
  • Experience working within Agile frameworks such as kanban and scrum, ideally using the Atlassian suite (Jira/Confluence)
  • Experience with compliance and regulatory requirements, e.g. GDPR, CCPA, SOX, PCI

• We are committed to creating and fostering a culture of inclusivity and diversity both on our teams and through our solutions.
  • We want people to feel comfortable bringing their whole selves to work, and to trust that they will be fully valued for who they are and what they can contribute.
  • We embrace progressive IT practices, prioritizing cloud and SaaS solutions over on-prem, agile over waterfall (or waterfall in disguise), and are always looking for a better way to solve, for our customers and ourselves
  • We're serious about the quality of the services we provide and believe in measuring our performance and striving to improve
  • And dogs in the office. Bring yours, too!

• In the greater Barcelona area the first-year salary range is €47,124 - €57,120. Additionally, Rover offers a long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout and benefits to full-time employees.
  • The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.
